title: Entities and Their Actions
summary: To exist is to be an entity of a specific nature. Action follows from what the entity is.

lessons.title: To be something
lessons.objective: Recognize that to exist is to be something, set against the nothing of nonexistence.

exercises.prompt: On this floor, what does it mean to exist?

choices.text: To be something
To be the nothing of nonexistence
To be whatever a wish names
To be only a word with no referent

feedback.note: Existence is being something. The nothing of nonexistence is what existence is set against, not a kind of thing that exists.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to what it names.

pairs.right: The nothing that is not a thing

feedback.note: The contrast is simple: existence is something, and nonexistence is not a hidden kind of something.

exercises.prompt: Finish the contrast.

feedback.note: The blank is something. Nothing, a wish, and a label do not name what existence is.

exercises.prompt: Which claim treats nonexistence as if it were a thing?

choices.text: Nothing is a special kind of entity
Nonexistence is what existence is set against
To exist is to be something
The nothing of nonexistence is not a something

feedback.note: Calling nothing a kind of entity erases the contrast. Nonexistence is the absence of a something, not another something.

exercises.prompt: Build the short claim in order.

feedback.note: The claim stops at something. Nothing and optional are the distractors, not part of the sentence.

exercises.prompt: A student says existence can be a pure blank, with no something in it. What is wrong?

choices.text: A blank is not a something, so it is not existence
A blank still counts as existing
Existence is weaker than being something
Being something starts only after a name is chosen

feedback.note: There is no existence that is not a something. A blank is the contrast, not a third option.

exercises.prompt: Match each mistake to the correction.

pairs.left: A word can exist with no referent
pairs.right: To exist is still to be something

feedback.note: Each correction returns to the same point: existence is being something, not a blank, a nothing, or a free-floating word.

exercises.prompt: Name the contrast and the requirement.

parts.text: of nonexistence, and it requires a

feedback.note: The first blank is the nothing of nonexistence. The second is the something that existence requires.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence stays on this lesson?

choices.text: If it exists, it is something
Causality is a separate primary beside identity
The senses are the only source of information
A right is a moral principle in a social context

feedback.note: This lesson only holds the contrast between something and the nothing of nonexistence. The other lines belong on other floors.

lessons.title: An entity
lessons.objective: Identify what exists as an entity, not as a loose feature floating free of any thing.

exercises.prompt: What kind of something does existence name here?

choices.text: An entity
A fog of features with no thing
A mood about the world
A rule that exists instead of things

feedback.note: To be something is to be an entity. Features, moods, and rules are not substitutes for the entity.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to how this lesson treats it.

pairs.left: Redness with no thing that is red
pairs.right: Not an entity on its own

pairs.left: A length with no thing that has it

feedback.note: The rock is the entity. Color and length are not extra things floating beside it.

exercises.prompt: Complete the claim.

parts.text: To exist is to be an
, not a feature cut loose from any thing.

feedback.note: The word for the something that exists is entity. A mood, a vote, or a blank is not that something.

exercises.prompt: Someone lists only colors, weights, and shapes, and says the entities can be dropped. What is missing?

choices.text: The entity those features belong to
A longer list of the same loose features
A prettier name for the list
Nothing; features can exist with no entity

feedback.note: Features are of an entity. Dropping the entity leaves a list that does not exist on its own.

exercises.prompt: Build the claim in order.

feedback.note: The sentence names an entity. Mood and fog are the wrong substitutes.

exercises.prompt: Which line keeps the entity in place?

choices.text: The redness is the redness of this apple
Redness exists even if no apple and no other thing is red
The apple can be deleted and the redness stays as a thing
Existence never reaches entities

feedback.note: The color is of the apple, which is the entity. It is not a second entity left behind when the apple is gone.

exercises.prompt: Match each starting point to the result.

pairs.right: Features have something to belong to

feedback.note: Entities are what exist. Features are identified only as features of those entities.

exercises.prompt: Fill both blanks.

parts.text: A weight is the weight of an

feedback.note: Weight belongs to an entity. It is not an entity of its own.

exercises.prompt: Why is a pile of labels not enough?

choices.text: The labels still have to name entities
Labels are the entities, so the things can go
An entity is less real than its name
Entities appear only after a theory is voted in

feedback.note: A label is not a substitute for the entity it is about. What exists is the entity.

lessons.title: A specific nature
lessons.objective: State that an entity has a specific nature, not an open character that can be anything.

exercises.prompt: What kind of nature does an entity have?

choices.text: A specific nature
Whatever nature a listener prefers
No nature at all
Every nature at once

feedback.note: An entity is something of a specific nature. Open, empty, and all-at-once natures are not that claim.

exercises.prompt: Match each entity to the nature this lesson keeps fixed.

feedback.note: Each entity has its own specific nature. One nature is not a blank you can hand to every entity.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit line.

parts.text: To exist is to be an entity of a

feedback.note: The nature is specific. Optional, voted, and blank deny that the entity is something in particular.

exercises.prompt: A student says a leaf can also be a stone while remaining the same entity. What fails?

choices.text: A leaf’s nature is not a stone’s nature
Specific natures are interchangeable
Only the names differ, so the natures match
Nature is assigned after the swap

feedback.note: Specific means this nature, not a costume. A leaf is not a stone, and calling it both does not change that.

exercises.prompt: Build the claim in order.

feedback.note: The sentence keeps nature specific. Optional and every pull it toward no nature or every nature.

exercises.prompt: Why is a nature with no character not a nature?

choices.text: Then the entity would not be anything in particular
A blank nature is still specific
Specific only means popular
A group can vote a blank into a nature

feedback.note: Specific nature is what makes the entity this something rather than a blank or anything else.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim to the verdict.

pairs.left: This flame has the nature of a flame
The flame is also solid ice in the same respect

feedback.note: A specific nature rules out both a blank and a contradiction of that nature.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two requirements.

parts.text: The something that exists is an entity, and that entity has a

feedback.note: Both words belong: the nature is specific. Optional and mood are not names for it.

exercises.prompt: Which question does this lesson answer?

choices.text: What kind of nature an entity has
How concepts omit measurements
Which rights a government may protect
What makes a work romanticist

feedback.note: The lesson is only about specific nature. Concept-formation, rights, and art schools are later floors.

lessons.title: Specific attributes
lessons.objective: Connect an entity’s nature to the specific attributes that make that nature up.

exercises.prompt: What is a specific nature made of?

choices.text: Specific attributes
Wishes about the entity
Votes about what it should be
Blanks with no character

feedback.note: Nature is not a tag pasted on afterward. It is made of the entity’s specific attributes.

exercises.prompt: Match each attribute to the entity it helps specify.

feedback.note: These attributes are examples of what makes each nature specific. They are not a full inventory of the entity.

exercises.prompt: Finish the line about nature.

parts.text: A specific nature is made of specific

feedback.note: The blank is attributes. Wishes, votes, and blanks do not make up a nature.

exercises.prompt: Which move separates attributes from the nature?

choices.text: Treating them as optional stickers on a blank entity
Treating them as what the nature is made of
Keeping them specific to this entity
Refusing to swap them for another entity’s attributes

feedback.note: Attributes are not decorations added to a nature that was already blank. They are the nature, specified.

exercises.prompt: Build the claim in order.

feedback.note: The sentence ends on attributes. Wishes and rumors are not what a nature is made of.

exercises.prompt: Two stones differ in size. What does this lesson still require?

choices.text: Each stone still has its own specific attributes
Different size means neither stone has attributes
Only the larger stone is an entity
Size cancels nature

feedback.note: A difference in an attribute does not erase attributes. Each entity remains something with its own specific ones.

exercises.prompt: Match each description to the status it has here.

pairs.left: A wish that the leaf be stone
pairs.right: Not an attribute of the leaf

pairs.left: A vote that the flame be cold
pairs.right: Not what the flame’s nature is made of

feedback.note: Attributes are of the entity. A wish or a vote does not become an attribute by being insisted on.

exercises.prompt: Fill both blanks.

feedback.note: Nature and attributes stay tied. Wishes and votes are the items that do not make up the nature.

exercises.prompt: What would a nature with no attributes be?

choices.text: Not a specific nature
A complete specific nature
A purer nature than one with attributes
A nature that gains attributes only by vote

feedback.note: Take the attributes away and nothing specific remains. A nature is made of them.

exercises.prompt: Where do the attributes sit?

choices.text: In the entity’s nature
Beside existence, as a second world
Only after someone describes them
Instead of the entity

feedback.note: Attributes are how the entity’s nature is specific. They are not a rival world, a later addition, or a replacement for the entity.

lessons.title: Action follows
lessons.objective: Explain that what an entity does follows from what that entity is, not from a demand that ignores its nature.

exercises.prompt: What does an entity’s action follow from?

choices.text: What the entity is
A wish that ignores what it is
A vote about what it ought to do
Nothing about the entity

feedback.note: Action follows from the entity. A wish, a vote, or a blank cause does not replace what the entity is.

exercises.prompt: Match each entity to an action that follows from what it is.

pairs.right: It can burn what will burn
It can fall as a solid body
It can dry and crumble as a leaf

feedback.note: The examples stay with each nature. The action is the kind of action that entity’s nature allows, not a demand from outside.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit’s second claim.

parts.text: Action follows from what the entity

feedback.note: The blank is is. Wishes, votes, and denials are not what the action follows from.

exercises.prompt: Someone demands that a stone burn as a flame burns, while remaining a stone. What is ignored?

choices.text: The stone’s specific nature
Nothing; any entity can do any action
Only the spelling of stone
A later vote that could rewrite the stone

feedback.note: The action of burning as a flame follows from a flame, not from a stone. The demand skips the nature.

exercises.prompt: Build the claim in order.

feedback.note: The sentence ties action to what the entity is. Wishes and nowhere do not belong in it.

exercises.prompt: Why can you not keep the entity and throw away the limits on its action?

choices.text: The limits come from the same nature that makes it that entity
Limits are an extra rule with no tie to the entity
Limits are only a mood about action
The entity is finished before any nature applies

feedback.note: What it can do is not taped on later. It follows from the specific nature the entity already is.

exercises.prompt: Match each demand to the fact it skips.

pairs.left: Make the flame solid like the stone
pairs.right: A flame is not a stone

pairs.left: Make the stone give light as the flame does
pairs.right: A stone is not a flame

pairs.left: Give the leaf no attributes and every action
pairs.right: A leaf is an entity of a specific nature

feedback.note: Each demand asks for an action that does not follow from that entity. The nature stays in place.

exercises.prompt: Hold both halves of the unit.

parts.text: An entity of a specific nature acts as that
allows, because action follows from what it

feedback.note: The two blanks keep the unit together: the nature, and what the entity is. Wish and vote are not either one.

exercises.prompt: Which pair states this unit and nothing beyond it?

choices.text: A specific entity, and action that follows from what it is
Percepts, then measurement-omission
Rights, then laissez-faire
Sense of life, then a school of art

feedback.note: This unit stops at the entity of a specific nature and the action that follows from it. The other pairs are other sections.

exercises.prompt: A cause with no entity behind the action would be which of these?

choices.text: An action cut off from what anything is
The ordinary case of action
A clearer account than one that starts from the entity
Just another name for specific nature

feedback.note: Action is of an entity. Drop the entity and there is nothing left whose nature the action could follow.
